summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for fever, weakness, and right upper quadrant pain. Evaluation revealed no source of infection on imaging or cultures, though wound cultures grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa resistant to ciprofloxacin and ceftazidime. He was treated with intravenous Cefepime, and Vancomycin was discontinued after 48 hours due to negative blood cultures. His abdominal ultrasound showed gallbladder sludge without cholecystitis. His chronic pain regimen was optimized by the pain service, reducing OxyContin and increasing gabapentin. Hypothyroidism was addressed by increasing levothyroxine from 88 to 100 mcg daily, and depression management was updated with an increased dose of venlafaxine. His heart function remained stable on metoprolol. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home with plans to restart oral antibiotics, begin ruxolitinib as part of a study, and follow up with multiple specialists.
